## d1c037cda16e

**Findings: advertised controls are silently ignored; self_check does not enforce its nine-color invariant.** Findings-only audit; no task or shared source changed. This is the immutable second draw in AUDIT_ASSIGNMENT.json. Generator SHA-256 is `d9f0a1782d0c3e9d5365e03779f8b58e876a1f2af751adf3f8dc62f9c68371b4`, matching the draw. Canonical program UTF-8 SHA-256 is `6ccc058b9b2eefbf6cbf155e33ddde07633fa68196b7b614a4ad407b24acd52b`. Supported Racket apply reported executed rule hash `2ddf73f57cad`, rule text SHA-256 `cde5477415a967ce06a1a4d366d36435cd973c61995fcb0306ccb083fc1d802e`, and `rule_hash_matches_catalog: true`. These are different named hash conventions, retained without conflation.

Scope: read the target generator, SUMMARY.md, notes.md, workspace README, empty associated_notes.jsonl, and only its canonical record. This target has no evidence/review_index.json. No solve, solve-blind, or private label contents were opened. Used a bounded review of 30 default generated inputs (seed 731; indices 0..9 independently in easy/medium/hard), nine exact override cases plus their baseline, three canonical training inputs, and two hand-made validator witnesses. No full battery or corpus-wide search was run.

### F1: dead exact controls and missing value validation

At seed `731`, sample index `0`, difficulty `medium`, changing `n_cells_per_block` from `1` to `3`, `fg_density` from `0` to `0.1`, or `decoy_density` from `0` to `0.05` leaves the input byte-for-byte equivalent as a JSON grid to the baseline. Every block still has exactly one nonzero cell. All six resulting grids pass `self_check` with `[]`. The source never consumes these three advertised AXES values. Their out-of-range value `999` is also accepted and ignored; an invalid texture string is accepted. This is an override-contract defect, independent of Racket correctness. The exact controls `palette_kind=all9`, `broad`, and `small` all produce all nine nonzero colors because the generator fills the proposed smaller pool with the remaining colors. The names therefore do not express an observable palette-size control, although they can change ordering. An advertised `block_h=1` is rejected at this medium-band setting with `override 1 outside [2, 4]`; the declared valid range is 1..6 and no incompatibility is stated in AXES.

These override and validator measurements are **Python-only diagnostics**, not Racket proof. Exact arguments, inputs, counts, exceptions, and validator results are in `diagnostic.json`; `probe.py` is the reproducer.

### F2: validator omission

The final `repeated-color-validator-witness` is a 6×6 zero grid with color `1` at coordinates `(0,0),(0,2),(0,4),(2,0),(2,2),(2,4),(4,0),(4,2),(4,4)`. It has one nonzero per block and just one foreground color. `self_check(grid, difficulty=None, meta={"texture":""})` returns `[]` despite INVARIANTS explicitly requiring nine different revealed colors. No degenerate-texture bypass is invoked. Supported Racket apply returns `[[1,1,1],[1,1,1],[1,1,1]]` without error. This is a validator/invariant mismatch; the witness is outside normal generated and canonical support, so it is not presented as a canonical-output error.

### Semantic support limitation, with actual Racket comparison

The last-nonzero rival agrees with the actual Racket output for all 43 generated/canonical inputs in this probe; a first-occurring-tie mode rival also agrees. Inspection explains the limitation: normal generation writes one nonzero into each block; optional anchor_first adds only the same color to block zero. The first/last policies cannot disagree anywhere on this nondegenerate generator support. Canonical examples also have one nonzero per block, so they do not establish an intended order policy for mixed blocks.

The `two-values-witness` has size 6×6, nonempty 2×2 blocks, all nine foreground colors, and passes `self_check` with `[]`. In block row-major order it places colors `1..9` at the top-left and `9..1` at the bottom-right. The rival predictions retained beside the actual Racket output in `comparison.json` are:

| Policy | Prediction |
| --- | --- |
| Actual Racket / first nonzero | `[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]` |
| Last nonzero rival | `[[9,8,7],[6,5,4],[3,2,1]]` |
| Mode, first-occurring tie | `[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]` |

This witness demonstrates the reference rule's operational order and the missing teaching support under advertised multi-cell controls. It is hand-made, has no generator seed/index, and lies outside the observed canonical one-cell-per-block domain. It does **not** establish a Racket defect or justify expanding the intended task domain. All 45 supported Racket applications succeeded; first-nonzero predictions matched all 45, last-nonzero matched 44. No canonical-output error found in the three canonical training checks.

### Exact reproduction and retained evidence

Working directory for every command: `/workspace/scratch/11eef787ff33/packet`.

1. `python3 checks/audit/d1c037cda16e/probe.py` — exit 0; writes `input.json` and `diagnostic.json`.
2. `python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply d1c037cda16e --input ../checks/audit/d1c037cda16e/input.json --out ../checks/audit/d1c037cda16e/racket.json` — exit 0; 45 grids, no errors. Apply refuses overwrite, so use a fresh output file for reruns.
3. `python3 checks/audit/d1c037cda16e/probe.py --compare` — exit 0; writes `comparison.json` containing rival predictions beside actual Racket results.

Evidence is under `checks/audit/d1c037cda16e/`. Review stops after reproducible contract defects and a supported operational witness; no universal induction or training approval is claimed.

triage.reason: Both findings-only audits read and transported in their task indexes. Targets unchanged. Independently reproduce pinned overrides or actual-reference witnesses before source repair; validator-only extension witnesses do not establish in-domain label defects.
